title: Twelfth Constable's History
full_text:
The Twelfth Constable spoke:

'A dishonest baker in the central market was suspected of short-weighting bread, but whenever the market inspectors tested his brass scale-weights, they weighed an exact standard pound on the dry balance.

Suspecting trickery, I brought a vessel of clear water and tested the weights by the ancient principle of water displacement: a solid pound of brass displaces an exact volume of water.

When the baker’s weight was placed in the water, it displaced far more water than solid brass should!

We drilled a tiny hole into the bottom: the center was hollowed out, lined with light pitch, and weighted with lead at the rim to balance dry scales while displacing volume!

The fraudulent baker was heavily fined, his shop given to an honest apprentice, demonstrating that science protects the poor from market extortion.'
moral: Science and testing physical volume expose the craftiest frauds in the marketplace.
